name: National Identity Card (DNI) number
issuer: the Ministry of Internal Affairs (General Directorate of Police)
note: Spain's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: for Spanish nationals the TIN is generally the National Identity Card (DNI) number, issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs (General Directorate of Police): 8 digits and a control letter (its rule isn't given, so `check` is left out). Foreigners use the NIE (X, Y or Z, seven digits and a letter), also from the Ministry, not modelled here; the Tax Administration gives a K number to resident Spaniards under 14 without a DNI, so the DNI is read as the citizen's number given on application. No age is set as `from` because the sheet doesn't state one. No fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Spain: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Natural persons of Spanish nationality: Generally, the TIN is the number on your National Identity Card, issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs (General Directorate of Police). ... 99999999L 8 digits + 1 control letter Spanish Natural Persons: DNI* ... K9999999L Letter K + 7 digits + 1 control letter Resident Spaniards under 14 without DNI*
